seed.title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

HP:0001030.label: Fragile skin
HP:0001030.text: skin fragility due to intraepidermal separation (epidermolysis bullosa simplex)

records.label: 38-year-old affected individual
quotes: The mutation, p.Gln1124X, leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and a complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e, as well as reduced labeling for plectin, the beta4 integrin subunit, and for type XVII collagen.

The 38-year-old affected individual has lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. In addition, he experiences episodic numbness in his limbs, which started at the age of 37 years.

These neurological symptoms may also be due to DST gene mutation, although he has a concomitant diagnosis of CADASIL (cerebral arteriopathy, autosomal dominant, with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy)

records.label: Five EBS patients from three families with bi-allelic DST mutations

phenotypes.text: skin fragility due to intraepidermal separation (epidermolysis bullosa simplex)

quotes: Mutation analysis revealed DST mutations in five patients belonging to three families. Two variants have not been previously reported: c.7097dupA (p.Tyr2366X) and c.7429delC (p.Leu2477Serfs*13).
Here, we report a series of EBS patients carrying bi-allelic DST mutations

notes.statement: Ganani et al. (2021) stated that DST-associated epidermolysis bullosa simplex is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: DST-associated EBS is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.

notes.statement: Ganani et al. (2021) reviewed 6 previously reported cases, bringing the total of individuals with EBS due to DST variants to 11, and found that patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.
quotes: We identified an additional six cases in the literature, bringing the total number of individuals affected with EBS due to DST variants to 11. Patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2012) reported autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to loss of expression of BPAG1-e.
quotes: Autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to loss of BPAG1-e expression.

notes.statement: Groves et al. (2010) found a homozygous nonsense mutation, p.Gln1124X, in the DST gene in a patient with an inherited skin fragility disorder. The mutation lies in the region that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230). The authors defined this as a new form of autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
quotes: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230).
the clinicopathological findings expand the molecular basis of EB by identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex.

notes.statement: In the patient's skin, Groves et al. (2010) found loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of BPAG1-e immunostaining. Immunolabeling for plectin, beta-4 integrin, and type XVII collagen was also reduced.
quotes: The mutation, p.Gln1124X, leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and a complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e, as well as reduced labeling for plectin, the beta4 integrin subunit, and for type XVII collagen.
